paras: The Himalayan keelback (Herpetoreas platyceps), also known commonly as the eastern keelback, is a species of snake in the subfamily Natricinae of the family Colubridae. The species is native to South Asia.
Herpetoreas platyceps is known from India along the sub-Himalayan region, Nepal, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Bhutan and China, at elevations of 1,040–4,000 m (3,410–13,120 ft).
The preferred natural habitat of Herpetoreas platyceps is forest near water, but it has also been found in disturbed areas such as agricultural fields and villages.

Herpetoreas platyceps has the following characteristics: Eye moderate; rostral just visible from above; suture between the internasals as long as that between the prefrontals or shorter; frontal longer than its distance from the end of the snout, shorter than the parietals; loreal longer than deep; one preocular (sometimes divided); two or three postoculars; temporals 1+1, or 1+2, or 2+2; 8 upper labials, third, fourth, and fifth entering the eye; 4 or 5 lower labials in contact with the anterior chin shields, which are much shorter than the posterior chin shields.
Dorsal scales in 19 rows, faintly or feebly keeled. 177-235 ventrals; anal divided; subcaudals 75–107, also divided.

Olive-brown above, with small black spots; frequently two black parallel lines or an elliptic marking on the nape; a light, black-edged streak on each side of the head, or a black line from eye to gape (corner of mouth); belly yellowish, with or without blackish dots; frequently a black line or series of elongate blackish spots along each side of the belly; lower surface of tail frequently mottled with blackish; throat sometimes black. In life, a coral-red band is said to run along the ends of the ventrals.
Total length 90 cm (3 feet); tail 23 cm (9 inches).
Herpetoreas platyceps is terrestrial, and it is active in the evening.
Herpetoreas platyceps preys upon a variety of small vertebrates, including fishes, frogs and their tadpoles, lizards, snakes and their eggs, birds, and mammals.
Herpetoreas platyceps is oviparous. Clutch size is 4–12 eggs. Each egg measures 8 mm × 25 mm (0.31 in × 0.98 in).
